correctness.rationale: For the finite weighted \(p\)-heat ODE, continuous monotone flux gives globally defined unique \(C^1\) solutions by monotonicity and boundedness. The difference of two solutions satisfies the coordinate maximum/minimum principle, so vertex oscillation contracts on all graphs. On a complete graph, edge Lipschitz equals oscillation. On every connected noncomplete graph, an induced \(j-i-k\) path and graph-distance perturbation \(h\) force an initially tight \(ij\) edge. At \(p>2\), put background \(R\) only at \(k\) and take \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) to obtain exact local rate \(c_{ik}(p-1)R^{p-2}/m_i\); as \(R\) grows this diverges. At \(1<p<2\), take equal background at \(i,k\) and generic distinct other backgrounds, giving \(c_{ik}\varepsilon^{p-2}/m_i+O(1)\) and divergence. These bounds prove the supremal liminf is infinite. The verified standalone checker performs an exact rational \(p=3\) witness, 78 noncomplete weighted finite cases and 132 complete-graph integrated samples; experiments are explicitly not the proof.

value.rationale: A motivated, complete structural classification of edge-Lipschitz *two-input* stability over every finite connected graph and every positive mass/conductance assignment, using graph completeness as an exact combinatorial criterion. It distinguishes vertex oscillation contraction from edge-gradient contractivity, and proves maximal-strength unbounded instantaneous growth for all other topologies. The induced-path isolation is a universal obstruction, not an arbitrary special graph slice; the theorem goes beyond known tree and cycle cases and supplies a natural theorem for stability analysis of nonlinear diffusion networks.
